Figures that don't agree: for the Ancien Régime, the page “Armorial des communes de l'Empire” speaks of forty towns enjoying the exclusive privilege of being represented by their mayors at the coronation; the page “Bonne ville” says bonnes villes were very numerous, with no official list, and only finds the number forty with the list of 1821. This chapter reports both, without reconciling them.
textes.Le point exact du centre de l'écu ; une: The exact centre of the shield; a single figure placed there is said to be en abîme.
textes.Se dit d'une figure principale que des f: Said of a main figure surrounded by secondary figures — beside, above or below it — placed perpendicular to it: “azure, a chevron or between three stars argent”. When the neighbouring figures follow the direction of the main one, French says accosté instead; when four of them fill out a cross or saltire, cantonné.
textes.Se dit d'une figure allongée — posée en: Said of an elongated figure — set palewise, bendwise or bendwise sinister — with other figures beside it, turned in the same direction. A round figure (bezant, ring) isn't flanked; if the neighbouring figures are turned differently, French says accompagné, and côtoyé when they are numerous.
textes.Émail métal représentant le blanc ; lais: Metal tincture representing white; left bare in engraving.
textes.Armoiries enfreignant volontairement la: Arms deliberately breaking the rule of tincture, which invites one to “enquire” into their history.
textes.Émail couleur, le bleu ; hachures horizo: Colour tincture, blue; horizontal hatching in engraving.
textes.Pièce honorable en diagonale, du chef de: Diagonal honourable ordinary, from dexter chief to sinister base.
textes.Pièce honorable en diagonale opposée à l: Honourable ordinary on the diagonal opposite the bend, from sinister chief to dexter base.
textes.Décrire des armoiries dans la langue tec: To describe a coat of arms in the technical language and agreed order of heraldry.
textes.Bande suivant le contour intérieur de l': A band following the inner outline of the shield.
textes.Modification légère d'armes pour disting: A slight change to arms to distinguish a branch or younger son of a family.
textes.Se dit d'un cheval dressé presque à la v: Said of a horse standing almost vertically on its hind legs. Effaré and effrayé are synonyms (some authors add forcené); effaré extends to other animals, but for the horse cabré is preferred.
textes.Petit carré posé à un angle de l'écu, au: A small square placed at a corner of the shield, in dexter chief unless stated otherwise. The canton is smaller than the franc-canton, itself smaller than the quarter (franc-quartier); authors disagree on the proportions, and two sevenths of the shield's width is often cited for the canton, a third for the franc-canton, half for the quarter. The word also refers to each of the four spaces left free by a cross or saltire — hence “cantoned”.
textes.Se dit d'une croix ou d'un sautoir dont: Said of a cross or saltire whose four free spaces — the cantons — are filled with secondary figures: the cross of Jerusalem is a cross potent between four small crosses.
textes.Le fond de l'écu, sur lequel se posent p: The background of the shield, on which ordinaries and charges are placed.
textes.Se dit d'une pièce ou d'un meuble sur le: Said of an ordinary or charge bearing other ordinaries or charges. The charged figure serves as a field: the charges take their usual place on it, unless the blazon says otherwise. To be distinguished from “over all” (brochant): the charge stays entirely within the figure bearing it, whereas a figure laid over all extends beyond.
textes.Tiers supérieur de l'écu, ou simplement: The upper third of the shield, or simply its upper part.
textes.Pièce en forme de compas ouvert, pointe: An ordinary shaped like an open pair of compasses, point towards the chief.
textes.Figure placée au sommet du heaume, au-de: A figure placed on top of the helm, above the shield.
The centre of the shield (see Fess point).
textes.Écu divisé horizontalement en deux parti: A shield divided horizontally into two equal parts.
textes.Pièce honorable formée par la rencontre: An honourable ordinary formed by the meeting of the pale and the fess.
textes.Le côté droit du porteur — donc la gauch: The bearer's right side — and so the viewer's left.
textes.Écu divisé en quatre quartiers par un tr: A shield divided into four quarters by a vertical and a horizontal line.
textes.Le bouclier, support des armoiries ; sa: The shield, the support of a coat of arms; its shape doesn't enter the blazon.
textes.Nom générique des teintes du blason : mé: The generic name for the hues of heraldry: metals, colours and furs.
textes.Pièce honorable horizontale occupant le: A horizontal honourable ordinary across the middle of the shield.
textes.Émail figuré par un semis conventionnel: A tincture shown by a conventional pattern: ermine, vair and their variants.
textes.Émail couleur, le rouge ; hachures verti: Colour tincture, red; vertical hatching in engraving.
textes.Fourrure d'argent semée de mouchetures d: A fur of argent semé of sable spots.
textes.Brisure en forme de barre à pendants, ma: A mark of difference shaped like a bar with points, the mark of the eldest son during his father's lifetime.
textes.Découpures feuillagées encadrant l'écu,: Foliate cut-outs framing the shield, derived from the helm's veil.
textes.Lion représenté passant, la tête de face: In French, a lion shown passant with its head facing out (lion passant guardant) — a question of posture, not species.
textes.Toute figure posée sur le champ hors des: Any figure placed on the field apart from the honourable ordinaries.
textes.Émail métal représentant le jaune ; poin: Metal tincture representing yellow; dotted in engraving.
textes.Bordure amincie détachée du bord de l'éc: A narrowed bordure detached from the edge of the shield.
textes.Pièce en forme d'Y : le bas du pal et le: A Y-shaped ordinary: the lower part of the pale and the upper halves of the bend and bend sinister, joined at the centre of the shield — three arms reaching the two corners of the chief and the base. Shortened and narrowed (“couped and pointed”), it corresponds to the shakefork of British heraldry, which has no name of its own in French.
textes.Pièce honorable verticale au milieu de l: A vertical honourable ordinary down the middle of the shield.
textes.Écu divisé verticalement en deux parties: A shield divided vertically into two equal parts.
textes.Grande figure géométrique traversant l'é: A large geometric figure crossing the shield (fess, pale, chevron, cross…).
textes.Se dit d'un écu d'un seul émail, sans me: Said of a shield of a single tincture, with no charge or ordinary: “argent plain” (more rarely champé d'argent). When only one part of a division is plain, the word can be left out. The Atelier writes plein.
The lower part of the shield.
textes.Émail couleur, le violet ; diagonales du: Colour tincture, violet; diagonals from sinister chief to dexter base.
textes.Se dit d'un animal dressé de profil sur: Said of an animal standing in profile on one leg, in an attacking posture.
textes.Se dit de meubles en nombre alignés dans: Said of several charges lined up in the direction of the ordinary named next: in fess (horizontally), in pale (vertically), in bend or in bend sinister (diagonally). The alignment doesn't set the position of each charge: three keys “ranged in fess” are lined up horizontally, each remaining palewise. Rangé en chef sums up “ranged in fess” placed in chief.
textes.Répétition d'une partition ou d'une pièc: Repetition of a simple division or ordinary over the whole field, giving striped fields (paly, barry…) and certain honourable ordinaries: “or, three pales gules”. Joubert, followed by this site's glossary, rather uses the word for the diminutive of a narrowed ordinary (barrulet, pallet, bendlet…); common usage calls that a diminished ordinary.
textes.Interdiction de poser métal sur métal ou: The ban on placing metal on metal or colour on colour, for legibility.
textes.Émail couleur, le noir ; hachures croisé: Colour tincture, black; crossed hatching in engraving.
textes.Croix posée en X, formée des deux diagon: A cross set as an X, formed by the two diagonals.
textes.Se dit d'un champ (d'écu, de partition o: Said of a field (of a shield, division or ordinary) in which a small charge is repeated many times, in no fixed number: the charges are drawn incomplete near the edges, as if continuing beyond, or disappear beneath the figures covering them. The field and the semé charges obey the rule of tincture: “azure semé of fleurs-de-lis or” (France ancient).
textes.Le côté gauche du porteur — donc la droi: The bearer's left side — and so the viewer's right.
textes.Émail couleur, le vert ; diagonales du c: Colour tincture, green; diagonals from dexter chief to sinister base.
textes.Figures (animaux, êtres) soutenant l'écu: Figures (animals, beings) holding up the shield on either side; in French, tenants if human.
textes.Dit seul, suivi d'un émail, c'est le rac: Said alone, followed by a tincture, this is short for “an escutcheon over all”: a small shield set at the centre of the main shield, on top of the rest, and read last. An escutcheon placed in turn on the first is “over all of all”. For another figure, one writes “a [charge] over all” (brochant sur le tout). Not to be confused with en abîme (a single figure at the central point, directly on the field) nor with “over all” for a figure passing across the whole.
textes.Écu divisé par la diagonale du chef sene: A shield divided by the diagonal from sinister chief to dexter base.
textes.Ce qui surmonte l'écu (heaume, couronne,: What surmounts the shield (helm, crown, mitre…) and marks rank.
textes.Écu divisé par la diagonale du chef dext: A shield divided by the diagonal from dexter chief to sinister base.
textes.Fourrure figurée par des clochettes alte: A fur shown by alternating bell shapes of argent and azure.
textes.Attitude d'un animal marchant à l'horizo: The attitude of an animal walking horizontally, its paws on the ground.
textes.Se dit d'un animal dont on ne voit que l: Said of an animal of which only the upper part is seen, as if emerging from an ordinary.
textes.Se dit d'un animal dont les griffes, cor: Said of an animal whose claws, horns or teeth are a different tincture.
textes.Se dit d'un animal dont la langue est d': Said of an animal whose tongue is a different tincture.
textes.Position ordinaire de l'aigle, ailes dép: The eagle's usual position, wings spread on either side.
textes.Se dit d'un oiseau dont les pattes sont: Said of a bird whose legs are a different tincture; beaked (becqué) for the beak.
textes.À deux têtes ; se dit surtout de l'aigle: With two heads; said above all of the imperial eagle.
textes.Merle stylisé sans bec ni pattes, souven: A stylised blackbird without beak or legs, often used as a mark of cadency.
textes.Créature chimérique mêlant l'avant de l': A chimerical creature combining the front of an eagle with the back of a lion.
textes.Croix dont les branches s'évasent aux ex: A cross whose arms flare at the ends.
textes.Croix dont les branches se terminent en: A cross whose arms end in anchor flukes.
textes.Figure de lune ; cornes en haut par défa: A moon figure; horns up by default, tourné, contourné or versé according to their direction.
textes.Figure rayonnante, à cinq rais dans l'us: A radiant figure, with five rays in French usage, six in English usage.
textes.Molette d'éperon : semblable à l'étoile: The rowel of a spur: similar to the star but pierced at its centre.
textes.Figure ronde et pleine, de métal (or ou: A solid round figure of metal (or or argent); a memory of the coins of the East.
textes.Figure ronde et pleine, de couleur — le: A solid round figure in a colour — the counterpart of the bezant, which is of metal.
textes.Fleur à cinq pétales, avec ses barbes (s: A flower with five petals, with its barbs (sepals) and seeds at the heart.
textes.Fleur héraldique à cinq pétales, sans ti: A heraldic flower with five petals, without stem or barbs.
textes.Lis stylisé à trois pétales liés d'une b: A stylised lily with three petals bound by a band; emblem of the kings of France.
textes.Se dit d'un meuble représentant une créa: Said of a charge representing an imaginary creature (dragon, griffin, unicorn).
textes.Ligne qui divise le champ ; sa direction: A line dividing the field; its direction (per pale, per fess…) and shape (wavy, engrailed…) are blazoned.
textes.Se dit d'un trait ou d'un bord tracé en: Said of a line or edge drawn in gentle waves.
textes.En créneaux carrés, à la manière du somm: With square crenellations, like the top of a wall.
textes.En grandes dents triangulaires ; le danc: In large triangular teeth; dancetty has only three or four, very prominent.
textes.Bordé de petits arcs dont les pointes mo: Edged with small arcs whose points bite outwards.
textes.Comme l'engrêlé, mais les petits arcs so: Like engrailed, but with the small arcs reversed (also called invecté).
textes.Trait en zigzag à grandes dents peu nomb: A zigzag line with few large teeth.
textes.Champ divisé en trois parts égales de tr: A field divided into three equal parts of three tinctures (in pale, in fess or in bend).
textes.Champ divisé en girons — triangles, le p: A field divided into gyrons — triangles, usually eight, meeting at the centre.
textes.Diviser à nouveau une partition existant: To divide an existing division again; great shields are composed by such further divisions.
textes.Trait en zigzag aigu, à angles rentrants: A line in a sharp zigzag, with re-entrant and salient angles.
textes.Se dit d'une pièce honorable raccourcie: Said of a shortened honourable ordinary that no longer touches the edges of the shield: “argent, a cross couped gules”. It then behaves like a charge. The Atelier can draw the fess, pale, bend, bend sinister, chevron and saltire couped; its couped cross is a charge.
textes.Se dit d'une figure qui prend naissance: Said of a figure that starts from a point or edge of the shield (chief, flank…) without occupying its full length.
textes.Champ couvert d'un nombre pair de bandes: A field covered with an even number of equal, alternating horizontal bands (a multiplied per fess). It is the name fascé takes from ten pieces, when they are thin.
textes.Champ couvert de pals alternés (multipli: A field covered with alternating pales (a multiplied per pale).
textes.Champ couvert de bandes parallèles alter: A field covered with alternating parallel bends (a multiplied per bend).
textes.Champ couvert de barres parallèles alter: A field covered with alternating parallel bends sinister (a multiplied per bend sinister).
textes.Fait de prendre les armes d'autrui — la: Taking another's arms — the only truly general ban in heraldic law; everything else is free.
textes.Règle coutumière qui tranche les conflit: A customary rule settling conflicts of arms in favour of the earliest bearer; formed under the Ancien Régime, it still holds.
textes.Armoiries inventées par l'administration: Arms invented by the royal administration between 1697 and 1710 to tax those who refused to declare theirs; nearly half of the Armorial général.
textes.Armoiries dont les meubles traduisent le: Arms whose charges turn the bearer's name into a rebus — Pinguet: a pine (pin) and a jay (geai).
textes.Armes retenues pour vérification en 1696: Arms held back for checking in 1696, notably those bearing fleurs-de-lis or on a field azure, subject to authorisation by the order of 22 July 1698.
textes.Quartier posé au canton dextre du chef ;: A quarter placed in the dexter corner of the chief; under the Empire it bears the mark of rank (azure for counts, gules for barons) and of office.
textes.Coiffure de velours noir à panache qui,: A black velvet headdress with a plume which, in Imperial heraldry, replaces the coronet of rank for all except the imperial family.
textes.Chapeau ecclésiastique à large bord qui: A broad-brimmed ecclesiastical hat ensigning the arms of clergy; its colour states the nature of the office, its tassels the dignity.
textes.Gland qui termine la cordelière du chape: The tuft ending the cord of the ecclesiastical hat; the higher the dignity, the more tassels.
textes.Coiffure à deux pointes des évêques et d: The two-pointed headdress of bishops and mitred abbots; removed from Catholic episcopal arms by the instruction of 31 March 1969, kept in the Church of England.
textes.Bâton pastoral à volute, symbole du Bon: A pastoral staff with a volute, symbol of the Good Shepherd and of jurisdiction; its heraldic use on episcopal arms was forbidden in 1969.
textes.Croix à hampe posée en pal derrière l'éc: A staffed cross set palewise behind the shield — one crossbar for a bishop, two for an archbishop, primate and patriarch.
textes.Bande circulaire de laine blanche chargé: A circular band of white wool charged with black crosses, characteristic of the arms of metropolitan archbishops.
textes.En Écosse, inscription d'armes existante: In Scotland, the entry of existing arms in the public register, after distinguishing them if need be with a difference; a judicial act of the Lord Lyon, open to appeal.
textes.Lord Lyon King of Arms, roi d'armes d'Éc: Lord Lyon King of Arms, Scotland's king of arms: he grants new arms, matriculates old ones and judges, on prosecution by a procurator fiscal, the illegal use of arms.
textes.Se dit d'une pièce — le chef surtout — d: Said of an ordinary — above all the chief — of metal on metal or colour on colour, held to be sewn to the field rather than placed on it, so as to escape the rule of tincture. Authors differ: Palliot (1664) extends the word to the other honourable ordinaries, Rietstap (1887) considers it useless, the fault being plain to see.
textes.Se dit d'une figure brochant sur un cham: Said of a figure over a field shared between two alternating tinctures: each part of the figure takes the tincture opposite to the ground it covers. This is the definition Wikipedia adopts for lack of consensus: authors distinguishing it from de l'un à l'autre don't agree on the sense of each, and Galbreath and Jéquier consider the distinction a chinoiserie.
textes.Se dit d'un meuble figuré dans sa couleu: Said of a charge shown in its real colour, outside the tinctures of heraldry; two special cases have their own name, carnation for flesh and tenné (tanné) for the brown of leather. Reserved for realistic charges — never the field, ordinaries or geometric charges.
textes.Se dit d'une pièce secondaire placée à l: Said of a secondary ordinary placed to the dexter of a main one; the word is also used of a shield whose dexter third has a different tincture from the field. Being ambiguous, “a dexter flank of…” is preferred: d'argent adextré de gueules is better blazoned “argent, a dexter flank gules”. The mirror term, senestré, is rarer still.
textes.Bande ou cotice réduite en largeur, norm: A bend or bendlet reduced in width, normally set bendwise (which goes unsaid); bendwise sinister, it is called bâton en barre. Used mainly as a mark of difference, often péri (shortened). Its definition varies by author: a bend or bend sinister reduced by half, a bendlet, or a bendlet shortened, raguly or flory, which then becomes a charge.
textes.Fasce diminuée, employée en nombre pair: A diminished fess, used in even numbers (four or more): “argent, six barrulets gules”. Alone, it is a divise; in odd numbers, a trangle; in twos, separated by a space equal to their width, a bar gemel (jumelle).
textes.Pièce honorable occupant le tiers inféri: An honourable ordinary occupying the lower third of the shield; diminished, it becomes a plaine. Not to be confused with the terrace, a charge with an irregular upper edge.
textes.Se dit d'un champ couvert d'un nombre pa: Said of a field covered with an even number of alternating chevrons, usually six or eight: “chevronny or and sable” (the original arms of Hainaut).
textes.Chevron étroit, réduit au tiers ou au qu: A narrow chevron, reduced to a third or quarter of its width — but sometimes wider, while staying thinner than the chevron. Almost a synonym of étai.
textes.Chef diminué, dit aussi « chef retrait »: A diminished chief, also called chef retrait. Wikipedia's list of ordinaries gives it sometimes as reduced to two thirds (sometimes half) of its height, sometimes to less than half.
textes.Se dit d'un champ divisé dans le sens de: Said of a field divided bendwise into more than eight pieces, as bendy has fewer; in the direction of the bend sinister, coticé en barre (or contre-coticé).
textes.Petite bande, réduite au tiers de sa lar: A small bend, reduced to a third of its width or repeated beyond four pieces; often used alone as a mark of difference. It is sometimes set bendwise sinister, fesswise or palewise, which is then stated. Thinner still, it is a filet. An ordinary flanked by bendlets is called cotised (coticée or côtoyée).
textes.Fasce diminuée, employée seule dans son: A diminished fess, used alone on its field (also spelt devise). Reduced by half according to one entry in Wikipedia's list, to less than a third according to another; its default place is that of the chief for Charles de Grandmaison, that of the fess for Pierre Palliot, who calls it divise en chef when it is at the top.
A common synonym of chevronel; for L.-A. Duhoux d'Argicourt, a small chevron supporting a charge, a view Wikipedia considers a minority one. Sometimes used in the feminine: une étaie.
textes.Se dit d'un champ divisé en un nombre pa: Said of a field divided into an even number of equal horizontal bands, of alternating tinctures: “barry of eight gules and argent” (Hungary). Six pieces by default, which goes unsaid; from ten, French says burelé.
textes.Cotice très diminuée, qui se pose en fas: A much diminished bendlet, set fesswise, palewise, bendwise or bendwise sinister — always stated. The filet en croix, or étrez, is a cross reduced to a filet.
textes.Bordure dont l'épaisseur est réduite à u: A bordure whose thickness is reduced to a filet.
textes.Pièce honorable qui correspond au bord d: An honourable ordinary corresponding to the dexter or sinister edge of the shield and extending to a third of it; rare.
textes.Carré posé en coin, légèrement plus gran: A square set in a corner, slightly larger than the canton and smaller than the quarter, in dexter chief by default; a third of the shield's width according to the values most often cited.
textes.Triangle rectangle qui a pour base la mo: A right-angled triangle whose base is half of one side of the field and whose opposite angle is at the centre of the shield; by default, the one issuing from the upper half of the dexter flank. Its shapes are those of a gyronny of eight.
textes.Pièce formée, en haut, d'un triangle mou: An ordinary formed, at the top, of a triangle issuing from the chief and joining, below, a pale. Its name comes from a piece of cloth, then from the metal piece linking the front and back of a suit of armour.
textes.Pièce formée de trois fasces alésées aux: An ordinary formed of three couped fesses with rounded or chamfered ends, held to be a single ordinary: “or, a hamaide gules”, arms of the Lords of La Hamaide (Belgium).
textes.Paire de burelles séparées par un espace: A pair of barrulets separated by a space equal to their width, the whole as thick as a fess. Usually fesswise, sometimes bendwise (which is then stated).
textes.Triangle isocèle dont la base, large des: An isosceles triangle whose base, two thirds of the shield's width, hangs from the chief and whose point aims downwards without reaching the bottom. Bendwise or bendwise sinister, it issues from a corner of the chief.
textes.Groupe de trois trangles séparées par un: A group of three trangles separated by a space equal to their width, the whole as thick as a fess; it is blazoned like the bar gemel.
textes.Fasce diminuée figurant toujours en nomb: A diminished fess always found in odd numbers. Alone, it is rather called a divise; in even numbers, barrulets.
textes.Pal réduit en largeur, rebattu cinq fois: A pale reduced in width, repeated five times or more.
textes.Se dit d'un champ divisé dans le sens du: Said of a field divided palewise into more than eight pieces (pallets), as paly has fewer.
textes.Se dit de deux écus posés côte à côte, o: Said of two shields set side by side, or leaning towards each other: the arms of a couple, the husband to dexter and the wife's father to sinister.
textes.Armes formées d'armes plus simples, acco: Arms formed of simpler arms, set side by side along a division or assembled in quarters. The division is stated, then each coat with its rank: “per pale, first… second…”.
textes.Armes d'un couple : deux écus côte à côt: The arms of a couple: two shields side by side or leaning towards each other, or a single shield per pale (husband to dexter, wife to sinister); quarterly for the line descending from the couple.
textes.Registre, tableau ou dictionnaire qui me: A register, table or dictionary matching names of families or communities with coats of arms, illustrated or only blazoned. Occasional, provincial, institutional and general armorials are distinguished.
textes.Pièce ou figure ajoutée aux armes princi: An ordinary or figure added to the main arms by grant, in honour of a title or an exploit: the chief of France of the bonnes villes, or the augmentations granted in England, notably to soldiers, in the 18th century.
textes.Modification d'un blason faite pour l'éq: A change to a coat of arms made for balance or harmony: turning the husband's lion to look at the wife's arms, reversing a bend into a bend sinister, reducing a charge to fit its quarter.
textes.Mot ou phrase de ralliement d'une armée: A rallying word or phrase of an army or company; in heraldry, it appears above the shield — the motto going below.
textes.Phrase courte qui suggère un idéal, une: A short phrase suggesting an ideal, a rule of conduct or a glorious past; in heraldry, usually on a scroll beneath the shield.
textes.Armoiries ornées de tous leurs ornements: Coats of arms adorned with all their external ornaments, generally a shield composed of quarters showing dependencies, with the owner's shield over all: a solemn assertion of titles and rights.
textes.Officier de l'office d'armes, chargé de: An officer of the office of arms, charged with solemn proclamations and messages, wearing the tabard, expert in arms. Four grades: king of arms, marshal of arms, herald, pursuivant.
textes.Ruban ou bandeau portant la devise ou le: A ribbon or band bearing the motto or war cry, usually beneath the shield, sometimes above or around it. The French word also, more rarely, means the bordure.
textes.Union de deux blasons par la moitié dext: The union of two coats of arms by the dexter half of one and the sinister half of the other. Not to be confused with coupé mi-parti, which the Wikipedia page advises avoiding.
textes.Armoiries funéraires, le plus souvent pe: Funerary arms, usually painted on a lozenge-shaped panel with a dark ground, with the year of death; an oval coat of arms for a wife or widow, a lozenge for a single woman.
textes.Chacune des divisions d'un écu partition: Each of the divisions of a divided shield — and, by extension, the arms it bears. They are numbered in reading order: top before bottom, dexter before sinister.
textes.Armes dont les figures évoquent le nom d: Arms whose figures evoke the bearer's name at one remove, without directly sounding it: a boar for a “Cochon” (pig), the tool of the trade for a guild.
textes.Dans la France d'Ancien Régime, ville pr: In Ancien Régime France, a town privileged by the king, bound to provide men-at-arms; it had the right to bear a chief of France in its arms. The status was recreated, as an honorific one, under the Empire and the Restoration (a list of forty towns in 1821).
textes.Couronne garnie de tours, symbole des mu: A crown fitted with towers, symbol of the walls of a fortified town; the Empire made it, with seven or five crenellations, the sign of towns' rank.
textes.Champ couvert de carreaux alternés de de: A field covered with alternating squares of two tinctures, like a chessboard: a paving, which the page “Champ composé” describes as an abutting semé of squares. It is counted in tires, its horizontal rows: a surface normally has about six, and the number is stated when it is clearly different (échiqueté de quatre tires). The Atelier draws six by default, from three to eight as chosen.
textes.Champ couvert de fusées (losanges allong: A field covered with abutting fusils (elongated lozenges), that is, touching at their points: an abutting semé of fusils, according to the page “Champ composé”. Called en bande or en barre, the fusils are set in that direction and each row traces the other diagonal. The Atelier draws a fusily of fixed proportions.
textes.Se dit d'un quadrupède représenté au gal: Said of a quadruped shown at a gallop: the two hind legs on the ground, the body horizontal. A stag in this attitude is rather called élancé.
textes.Se dit d'un animal au tronc allongé, la: Said of an animal with its body stretched out, the head remaining raised (for a stag, gisant); when the head also rests on the ground, it is dormant.
textes.Se dit d'un animal dont l'arrière-train: Said of an animal whose hindquarters rest on the ground and whose body is upright, its forepaws also on the ground; raised, they make it accroupi.
textes.Se dit d'un oiseau dont les ailes, décol: Said of a bird whose wings, away from the body, have their feathers pointing downwards: an eagle with wings lowered.
textes.Dragon à deux pattes, que l'héraldique b: A two-legged dragon, which British heraldry distinguishes from the four-legged dragon. The word comes from the Anglo-French wivre, “viper”, like the French guivre.
textes.Draperie de couleur, généralement doublé: A coloured drapery, generally lined with ermine (with vair for Dukes of the Empire), falling around the shield: an attribute of the sovereign, princes and dukes. That of the peers of France was azure. Drawn with the holder's arms on its side parts, or in the colours of the shield.
textes.Tente qui coiffe le manteau et le distin: A tent topping the mantle and setting it further apart: reserved for the sovereign alone, it marks the summit of the hierarchy.
textes.Rangée horizontale de pièces répétées da: A horizontal row of repeated pieces in a composite field (chequy, vairy, semé): échiqueté de six tires.
textes.Se dit d'une pièce entourée d'une bordur: Said of an ordinary surrounded by a border of a different colour, a narrow edging: “a cross argent fimbriated gules”.
textes.Se dit de deux clefs dont les anneaux so: Said of two keys whose rings are intertwined.
textes.Se dit de deux clefs (ou épées, lances): Said of two keys (or swords, spears) crossed in an X; on papal arms, one is or, the other argent.
textes.Se dit de deux clefs en sautoir dont les: Said of two keys in saltire whose rings are joined by a tie.
textes.Pour la tête de sanglier, si la défense: For a boar's head, if the tusk is a different tincture, it is tusked (défendue de…); if the eye, it is eyed (allumée de…).
textes.Se dit d'un arc dont la corde est d'un a: Said of a bow whose string is a different tincture; the arms of Ireland likewise describe the harp as “or stringed argent”.
textes.Se dit de la ramure d'un cerf quand elle: Said of a stag's antlers when a different tincture from the body; ramé, chevillé or sommé de dix cors also state the number of points. A stag's head seen from the front is a rencontre.
textes.La flèche se compose d'un fût, d'une poi: An arrow consists of a shaft, a point and feathers. When the point is a different colour, it is armed or barbed (armée, ferrée); when the feathers are, it is flighted (empennée); when the shaft is, it is fûtée. Set alone, it is palewise, point up; point down, it is versée.
textes.Tête d'animal vue de face, sans cou : la: An animal's head seen from the front, without a neck: a stag's head from the front is a rencontre de cerf. Wikipedia's list gives the word only for the stag; the figures of Commons' Projet:Blasons also use it for the bear, wolf, lion, leopard, ram and boar.
textes.Se dit d'une figure qui porte une autre: Said of a figure bearing another figure at its summit (“an anchor topped by a crescent”, “a bridge topped by a castle”). For a stag, antlers of a particular tincture are called ramée or sommée, and sommé de dix cors counts its points.
textes.Se dit d'une figure qui porte au-dessus: Said of a figure bearing another figure above it: a Noah's ark “surmounted by a house”, a building “surmounted by a weathervane” (it is then girouetté).
textes.Se dit d'un arbre planté sur une terrass: Said of a tree planted on a terrace, normally issuing from the base of the shield.
textes.Petit écu d'armoiries posé dans l'écu («: A small shield of arms placed within the shield (“argent, charged with an escutcheon gules”). Set at the heart of a quarterly shield, it is called “overall”.
textes.Colonne grecque d'ordre ionique au trait: A Greek column of the Ionic order in a simplified line, without volute, ovolo, fluting or torus (“argent, a column gules”).
textes.Le bras, droit (dextrochère) ou gauche (: The arm, right (dextrochère) or left (senestrochère). Bare by default, it can be clothed (paré) or armoured (armé), and often issues from a flank, which must then be blazoned.
textes.Se reconnaît à ses pis ; généralement pa: Recognised by its udder; generally passant, the tail stretched along the flank. The arms of Béarn bear two: “or, two cows gules, horned, collared and belled azure”.
textes.Le navire de base comprend une coque sim: The basic ship has a simple hull, a mast and a sail; it can be rigged, its sails filled (“azure, a ship argent”). The oared ship (longship, drakkar) represents royal power in ancient Scottish heraldry; the galley has sails that are always furled.
textes.Griffes, serres, cornes ou dents d'un au: Claws, talons, horns or teeth in a different tincture from the body.
textes.La langue d'un autre émail ; on dit auss: The tongue in a different tincture; also langué.
textes.L'œil d'un autre émail ; se dit aussi d': The eye in a different tincture; also said of a flame or a grenade.
The beak in a different tincture.
A bird's legs in a different tincture.
textes.Les sabots fourchus d'un autre émail — c: The cloven hooves in a different tincture — stag, bull, hind, unicorn.
The horns in a different tincture.
textes.Porte un collier ; bouclé si le collier: Wearing a collar; bouclé if the collar has its buckle. The greyhound always is.
textes.Porte une clarine, la clochette du bétai: Wearing a clarine, the bell of cattle.
textes.Porte une couronne, le plus souvent d'un: Wearing a crown, usually in a different tincture.
The sex visible and in a different tincture.
textes.La crête et la barbe du coq d'un autre é: The comb and wattles of a cock in a different tincture.
textes.Les ocelles de la queue du paon d'un aut: The eyespots of a peacock's tail in a different tincture.
The base of the neck in a different tincture — rare.
textes.Les nageoires, la queue et les ouïes du: The fins, tail and gills of a dolphin.
textes.Les glands du chêne d'un autre émail ; o: The acorns of an oak in a different tincture; also englandé.
textes.La tige, les feuilles ou les fruits d'un: The stem, leaves or fruit of a plant in a different tincture.
textes.Le cœur et les sépales d'une rose d'un a: The heart and sepals of a rose in a different tincture.
textes.Le tronc de l'arbre d'un émail particuli: The trunk of a tree in a particular tincture.
textes.Les joints de pierre d'un bâtiment appar: The stone joints of a building visible and in a different tincture.
textes.Les fenêtres et la porte d'un autre émai: The windows and door in a different tincture — and so empty.
textes.Le toit du même émail, ou d'un émail dif: The roof in the same tincture, or in a different one.
textes.Surmonté d'une ou plusieurs tourelles ;: Surmounted by one or more turrets; the number is blazoned.
textes.La porte munie d'une herse, ouverte ou b: The door fitted with a portcullis, open or lowered.
textes.Surmonté d'une girouette en forme de pen: Surmounted by a weathervane shaped like a pennon or banner.
textes.Les anneaux, l'embouchure, le pavillon o: The rings, mouthpiece, bell or strap of a horn.
textes.Le battant de la cloche d'un autre émail: The clapper of a bell in a different tincture.
textes.Les plumes, le fer et la hampe de la flè: The feathers, head and shaft of an arrow.
textes.Entouré d'un nimbe — saints, anges, agne: Surrounded by a nimbus — saints, angels, paschal lamb.
textes.L'eau d'une fontaine d'un autre émail ;: The water of a fountain in a different tincture; the number of jets is blazoned.
textes.Dressé de profil sur une patte arrière,: Standing in profile on one hind leg, one foreleg raised — the lion's default position.
textes.Marchant à l'horizontale, les pattes pos: Walking horizontally, its paws on the ground.
textes.Passant et la tête tournée vers le spect: Passant with the head turned towards the viewer — which makes the lion a French “leopard”.
textes.Inverse du précédent : un léopard dressé: The reverse: a leopard standing like a lion.
textes.On n'en voit que la partie supérieure, c: Only the upper part is seen, as if emerging from an ordinary or the edge.
textes.Sortant du milieu du champ ou d'une lign: Emerging from the middle of the field or from a line of division.
textes.Dressé sur ses pattes arrière — se dit s: Rearing on its hind legs — said above all of the billy goat and the ram.
A horse standing on its hind legs.
textes.Le taureau dressé, la queue relevée au-d: A bull rearing, its tail raised above its back.
textes.Le chat ou le taureau représenté rampant: A cat or bull shown rampant.
A wolf or fox raised like a lion.
textes.Le chat faisant le gros dos, les pattes: A cat arching its back, its paws drawn together.
textes.Le cerf courant, les antérieurs ne touch: A stag running, its forelegs no longer touching the ground.
textes.Les quatre pattes à terre — position ord: All four feet on the ground — the elephant's usual position.
textes.Le corps presque à la verticale ; se dit: The body almost vertical; said of the bear.
textes.Assis — position non naturelle, employée: Sitting — an unnatural position, used for the horse and the unicorn.
textes.Tourné vers senestre alors que la positi: Turned to sinister when the default position looks to dexter.
textes.Les ailes ouvertes et étendues — l'aigle: The wings open and spread — the eagle from the 16th century.
textes.Les ailes ouvertes et coudées — l'aigle: The wings open and bent — the medieval eagle.
textes.Prenant son envol, ou déjà en train de v: Taking flight, or already flying; descending towards the base, fondant if it dives.
textes.Le rapace tenant quelque chose entre ses: A bird of prey holding something in its talons.
A peacock facing out, spreading its tail.
textes.Le poisson posé en fasce ; couché, versé: A fish set fesswise; couché, versé, pâmé as the case may be.
textes.La gueule béante — un dauphin ou un pois: With gaping mouth — a dolphin or fish without visible teeth or tongue.
textes.Privé de bec, de pattes, de griffes ou d: Deprived of beak, legs, claws or tongue — the martlet is so by definition.
textes.Prenant naissance à un bord ou à un poin: Starting from an edge or point of the shield without entirely occupying it.
textes.Passant par-dessus d'autres figures, qu': Passing over other figures, partly covering them.
textes.Agneau passant, la tête contournée, tena: A lamb passant, head turned back, holding a banner with a cross; often nimbed.
textes.Mouton aux cornes en spirale ; dressé, i: A sheep with spiral horns; rearing, it is salient.
textes.Debout ou assise, souvent d'or ou d'arge: Standing or sitting, often or or argent, sometimes pierced by an arrow.
textes.Passant, de profil, la queue pendante en: Passant, in profile, the tail hanging between the legs.
textes.Représenté entier et dans des positions: Shown whole and in upright positions, tail raised.
textes.Reconnaissable à ses pis, la queue étend: Recognisable by its udder, the tail stretched along the flank.
textes.Chèvre alpine à très grandes cornes ; le: An alpine goat with very large horns; the chamois has thin ones, with spatulate tips.
textes.Ramé, chevillé ou sommé de N cors, répar: Attired (ramé, chevillé) or topped with N points, arranged symmetrically; élancé when running.
textes.Se distingue du cerf par des bois plus l: Distinguished from the stag by wider, flattened antlers.
textes.Le bois du cerf ; demi-ramure pour un se: The stag's antlers; demi-ramure for just one of the two.
textes.Crâne de cerf vu de face avec ses bois —: A stag's skull seen from the front with its antlers — not to be confused with a rencontre.
textes.Tête d'un quadrupède vue de face ; ni le: A quadruped's head seen from the front; neither lion nor leopard has one, by definition.
textes.Tête de sanglier — également de dauphin: The head of a boar — also of a dolphin or salmon — seen in profile.
textes.Toujours la tête de face ; hérissonné qu: Always with its head facing out; hérissonné when arching its back.
textes.Gai quand il est sans harnais ; sellé, b: Gai when without harness; otherwise saddled, bridled, caparisoned, rearing or kicking.
textes.Reconnaissable à sa barbiche et à ses co: Recognisable by its goatee and straight horns; a rearing billy goat is salient.
textes.La race se blasonne si elle est reconnai: The breed is blazoned if recognisable: greyhound, mastiff, pointer.
textes.Toujours colleté ; le levron est sans co: Always collared; the levron has no collar, the levrette is the female.
textes.De profil, souvent mangeant, la queue re: In profile, often eating, the tail rising above the head.
textes.Arrêté sur ses quatre pattes ; défendu q: Standing on all four legs; tusked (défendu) when its tusks are a different tincture.
textes.Le petit carnassier lui-même, d'argent e: The small carnivore itself, argent and passant; in sable, it is the sable (zibeline).
textes.Nom que prend le lion dès qu'il figure e: The name a lion takes as soon as it appears in numbers on the shield.
textes.Passant, la queue pendante ; ravissant q: Passant, tail hanging; ravissant when raised like a lion.
textes.Comme le loup, mais la queue dressée — c: Like the wolf, but with the tail raised — that is what tells them apart.
textes.Deux figures distinctes ; le lynx passe: Two distinct figures; the lynx is passant or faces out, a symbol of perspicacity.
textes.Tête plate, queue courte, griffes fortes: Flat head, short tail, strong claws; muzzled (emmuselé) when wearing a muzzle.
textes.De profil, la queue recercelée ; flamboy: In profile, the tail curled; flamboyant if flames come from its eyes.
Set palewise and seen from behind.
textes.Poisson serpentiforme au corps toujours: A serpent-like fish with an always undulating body.
textes.Ancien nom du barbeau ; allongé, en pal: An old name for the barbel; elongated, palewise and curved, often in pairs and addorsed.
textes.Poisson à grosse tête, en pal, vu de dos: A big-headed fish, palewise, seen from behind, with two fins on each side.
textes.Compté parmi les poissons ; arqué, hure: Counted among fish; arched, head and tail to dexter; pâmé with gaping mouth.
textes.Poisson dont la tête isolée se nomme hur: A fish whose separate head is called a hure.
textes.Montante, vue de dos, pattes étendues, a: Rising, seen from behind, legs spread, wings half open; volante if open.
textes.Nom héraldique de la libellule, de profi: The heraldic name for the dragonfly, in profile and flying bendwise.
textes.Escargot de profil issant de sa coquille: A snail in profile emerging from its shell, horns visible.
textes.Posée de front, les ailes étendues ; fré: Set facing out, wings spread; frequent as an Aragonese crest.
textes.Petite aigle, presque toujours employée: A small eagle, almost always used in numbers.
textes.Aiglon stylisé sans bec ni serres, le po: A stylised eaglet without beak or talons, the breast visible, wings spread.
textes.Oiseau de mer représenté dans son nid fl: A sea bird shown in its nest floating on the waves.
textes.De profil, les ailes serrées, tourné ver: In profile, wings closed, turned to dexter.
textes.Petit oiseau au jabot proéminent ; armé,: A small bird with a prominent crop; armed, unlike the martlet, which is morné.
textes.De profil, la tête de face ; sans aigret: In profile, the head facing out; without ear tufts, which distinguishes it from the hibou.
textes.Rapace nocturne dont la tête porte des a: A nocturnal bird of prey with ear tufts on its head; variants duc and grand-duc.
textes.Crête, barbe et plumes du col ; hardi un: Comb, wattles and neck feathers; hardi with one foot raised, crowing with its beak open.
textes.Se distingue de l'aigle par son bec droi: Distinguished from the eagle by its straight beak and non-heraldic position.
textes.Chaperonné s'il est capuchonné, longé pa: Hooded (chaperonné), jessed (longé), belled (grilleté).
textes.Rouant quand il fait la roue de face ; m: In its pride (rouant) when spreading its tail facing out; miraillé if its eyespots differ.
textes.Dans son aire, se perçant la poitrine po: In its nest, piercing its breast to feed its young: its “piety”.
Rather plump, with a short beak.
textes.Le nid de certains oiseaux — pélican, cy: The nest of certain birds — pelican, swan, eagle.
textes.Paire d'ailes jointes à l'articulation ;: A pair of wings joined at the joint; a single wing is a demi-vol.
textes.Créature composite proche du griffon, pr: A composite creature close to the griffin, almost solely in English arms.
textes.Dragon dont la queue en volute se termin: A dragon whose coiled tail ends in a second serpent's head.
textes.Armé d'une massue par défaut ; le centau: Armed with a club by default; the centaur-sagittary shoots a bow.
A three-headed dog, guardian of the underworld.
textes.Tronc de femme, serres d'aigle en guise: A woman's torso, eagle's talons for arms, a goat's body, a serpent's tail.
textes.Serpent dont le corps forme plusieurs vo: A serpent whose body forms several coils.
textes.Figure composite rattachée à la famille: A composite figure belonging to the eagle family.
textes.Tête de carnation semée d'yeux — l'homme: A flesh-coloured head covered with eyes — the man nothing can deceive.
textes.Touffu et laissant voir ses racines ; ar: Bushy and showing its roots; arraché, terrassé, futé, étagé, écoté or tronqué.
textes.Feuilles et glands dessinés un à un ; en: Leaves and acorns drawn one by one; englanté if the acorns differ.
textes.Arbre stylisé à sept branches terminées: A stylised tree with seven branches ending in pike heads, on a few roots.
textes.Ramure symétrique, les extrémités recour: Symmetrical branches, the ends curving towards the chief.
textes.Tronc large et branches multiples, fines: A broad trunk and many thin, leafy branches.
textes.Tronc d'arbre dont les branches ont été: A tree trunk with its branches cut off.
textes.Bâton noueux, à distinguer de l'écot qui: A knotty stick, to be distinguished from the écot, which shows a trunk.
textes.Fleur imaginaire de quatre à dix pétales: An imaginary flower of four to ten petals, pierced at the centre, without stem or leaves.
textes.Trois noisettes réunies par leurs cupule: Three hazelnuts joined by their husks, one towards the chief.
textes.Fruit ouvert laissant voir ses grains, l: An open fruit showing its seeds, the stalk downwards.
textes.Le lis de jardin, bien distinct de la fl: The garden lily, quite distinct from the heraldic fleur-de-lis.
textes.Sarment feuillé et fruité de grappes ; l: A leafy shoot bearing bunches of fruit; the vine stock is shown with its stake.
textes.En fasce ou en bande, burelé d'or, de gu: Fesswise or bendwise, barruly or, gules, vert and argent, issuing from the edges.
textes.Tête d'enfant joufflu soufflant le vent: A chubby child's head blowing the north wind, the blasts in the same tincture.
textes.Arrondie par le bas, terminée en jets on: Rounded at the bottom, ending in wavy tongues; most often gules.
textes.Masculin en héraldique : deux faisceaux: Masculine in French heraldry: two opposed bundles of flames and darts in saltire.
textes.Rarement pleine ; en croissant ou en déc: Rarely full; crescent or waning, shown with a human profile.
textes.Figuré quand il porte un visage ; non fi: Figuré when it has a face; otherwise non figuré, éteint, éclipsé, levant or couchant.
textes.Rayon du soleil, pointe d'étoile ou de m: A ray of the sun, point of a star or rowel, spoke of a wheel, point of an antique crown.
textes.Toujours mouvante de la pointe, occupant: Always issuing from the base, occupying the lower third of the field.
textes.Terme discuté, tenu pour un synonyme de: A debated term, held to be a synonym of river and to be used with caution.
textes.Chacune des fasces ondées qui traversent: Each of the bars wavy crossing a heraldic fountain.
textes.Uni par défaut, mais le plus souvent en: Plain by default, but most often in hillocks (coupeaux) whose number is blazoned.
textes.Un des mamelons du mont, arrondi en pain: One of the hillocks of a mount, rounded like a sugar loaf; never used alone.
textes.Sol mouvant de la pointe ; isolée si ell: Ground issuing from the base; isolée if it doesn't touch the edge.
textes.Posée en pal, le manche vers le bas ; el: Set palewise, the stock downwards; it shoots bolts (carreaux).
textes.En pal, la corde à dextre ; couché quand: Palewise, the string to dexter; couché when fesswise, stringed if the string differs.
textes.Armée par son fer, empennée par ses plum: Armed by its head, flighted by its feathers, fûtée by its shaft; versée, encochée.
textes.Cimeterre à lame courte et large, recour: A scimitar with a short, broad blade, curved towards the point.
textes.Synonyme d'épée ; l'épée est en pal, poi: A synonym of sword; the sword is palewise, point up, dégarnie without its guard.
textes.Hampe élargie à la base pour protéger la: A staff widened at the base to protect the hand; brisée, émoussée, fûtée, armée.
textes.Arme d'hast à hampe cylindrique, ce qui: A polearm with a cylindrical staff, which distinguishes it from the lance.
textes.Bout de fer de pique, dit aussi amande p: The end of a pike head, also called a peeled almond; four in saltire make the cross of Comminges.
textes.Garniture métallique de l'extrémité d'un: The metal fitting at the end of a sword's scabbard.
textes.Pièce d'artillerie, affûtée d'un autre é: A piece of artillery, its carriage in another tincture; couleuvrine in the Middle Ages.
textes.Bombe sphérique à mèche, allumée de gueu: A spherical bomb with a fuse, lit gules; éclatante when exploding.
textes.Poteau garni de barreaux et terminé par: A pole fitted with rungs and ending in a hook.
textes.Bâton ailé entouré de deux serpents entr: A winged staff entwined by two serpents; a symbol of medicine.
textes.Normalement ouverts en sautoir ; meuble: Normally open in saltire; a mainly burgher and craftsman's charge.
textes.Paire de lames reliées par un ressort, p: A pair of blades linked by a spring, for shearing; renversées point down.
textes.Hachette à manche court et lame en demi-: A hatchet with a short handle and a half-moon blade, the handle set bendwise.
textes.Présentée le fer en haut, pointant à dex: Shown blade up, pointing to dexter.
textes.Même présentation que la faucille ; outi: Shown like the sickle; a late tool, appearing in the 16th century.
textes.Deux courbes en C adossées, liées par de: Two addorsed C curves, linked by crossbars; often confused with the millrind.
textes.Couteau de bois à briser la tige du chan: A wooden knife for breaking the stems of hemp and flax, often in pairs.
textes.Pince à maîtriser les chevaux par les na: Pincers for controlling horses by the nostrils; confused with the broyes.
textes.De labour, tronconique ; sarrasine quand: For ploughing, a truncated cone; sarrasine for the portcullis of a gate.
textes.Instrument à enfoncer les pavés, en fusé: A tool for ramming paving stones, like a long fusil with two annulets; rare.
textes.Poignée de bois à deux cordes, qui serva: A wooden handle with two cords, used to tie hunting dogs in pairs.
textes.Bâton de pèlerin à pommeau ; insigne des: A pilgrim's staff with a knob; the insignia of dignitaries with no right to the crozier.
textes.Se blasonne ajouré, ouvert, maçonné, cou: Blazoned ajouré, ouvert, maçonné, couvert, essoré, girouetté, hersé or coulissé.
textes.Forteresse à plusieurs tours ; donjonné: A fortress with several towers; donjonné when turrets surmount it.
textes.Portion de muraille flanquant une tour,: A section of wall flanking a tower, issuing from a flank of the shield.
textes.Voûté, d'une ou plusieurs arches ; gardé: Vaulted, with one or more arches; gardé when turrets occupy its ends.
textes.Pont à nombreuses arches, soumis aux mêm: A bridge with many arches, subject to the same rules as the bridge.
textes.Colonne grecque d'ordre ionique, au trai: A Greek column of the Ionic order, in a simplified line.
textes.Coque, mât et voile ; équipé, habillé, l: Hull, mast and sail; rigged (équipé, habillé), the sails filled or furled.
textes.Navire équipé et habillé, comme dans les: A rigged and dressed ship, as in the arms of Paris.
textes.Navire antique aux voiles toujours ferlé: An ancient ship with sails always furled, much used in English arms.
textes.Disque ombré, ce qui la distingue du bes: A shaded disc, which distinguishes it from the bezant and torteau, both flat.
textes.Petit sac à coulisse ; liée quand le fil: A small drawstring bag; liée when the cord is a different tincture.
textes.Pièce à battre le silex ; celui de Const: A piece for striking flint; that of Constantinople is confused with a capital B.
textes.Coupe eucharistique, souvent surmontée d: A eucharistic cup, often surmounted by a host.
textes.Carré posé sur un côté ; huppé aux angle: A square set on one side; tufted at the corners, it is better blazoned as a cushion.
textes.Marmite à trois pieds et une anse, dite: A pot with three feet and one handle, also called a marmite à cornière.
A three-legged pot, without a handle.
textes.La partie d'azur de la fourrure, évasée: The azure part of the fur, flared at the bottom; the rest is the argent pot.
textes.En pal, l'anneau en pointe et le panneto: Palewise, the ring in base and the ward in chief turned to dexter; interlaced, bound.
textes.Meuble à part entière, ornement extérieu: A charge in its own right, the external ornament of an order, or an attribute of a collared animal.
textes.Petit cor de chasse dépourvu d'attache —: A small hunting horn without a strap — that is what distinguishes it from the horn.
textes.Grand cor de chasse, celui du chevalier: A large hunting horn, the knight's; Roland's oliphant.
textes.Employée comme meuble, souvent très styl: Used as a charge, often highly stylised; a fragment set bendwise is a crancelin.
textes.Fragment de couronne à fleurons posé en: A fragment of a crown with fleurons set bendwise, from the arms of Saxony.
textes.Anneau unique posé dans l'écu ; terme dé: A single ring set on the shield; an obsolete term.
textes.Petit écu posé sur le champ ; sur le tou: A small shield set on the field; overall when laid at the heart of a quarterly.
textes.Bâton surmonté d'une flamme ; allumé qua: A staff topped by a flame; allumé when the flame is a different tincture.
textes.Eau coulant dans des vasques ; jaillissa: Water flowing in basins; jaillissante if the water is a different tincture.
textes.Nœud de corde dont la forme varie tant q: A knot of cord whose shape varies so much that it is better to name the knot.
textes.Ouvert ou fermé, parfois chargé de lettr: Open or closed, sometimes charged with letters such as alpha and omega.
textes.Boule cintrée d'une bande et croisettée: A ball banded and topped with a cross — universal sovereignty.
textes.Gibet ; jugée trop sinistre, elle a parf: A gallows; thought too grim, it was sometimes replaced by a tau.
textes.Roue de Mayence à six rayons, roue de mo: The wheel of Mainz with six spokes, a mill wheel, or a paddle wheel.
textes.Attribut de souveraineté ; le diadème en: An attribute of sovereignty; the diadem is its counterpart for the head.
textes.Cerclé quand ses cercles sont d'un autre: Cerclé when its hoops are a different tincture.
textes.Double bourse de cuir servant à porter l: A double leather bag for carrying water; also called bouse, bouge or bougette.
textes.Figuré en jeune fille vêtue d'une dalmat: Shown as a young girl wearing a dalmatic, the wings almost always lowered.
textes.Ange aux traits d'enfant ; le chérubin n: An angel with a child's features; the chérubin is only a head surrounded by wings.
textes.Cupidon en enfant ailé, muni d'un arc et: Cupid as a winged child, with a bow and quiver.
textes.Dextrochère ou senestrochère ; nu par dé: Dexter or sinister arm; bare by default, clothed or armoured.
textes.Tête, cou et poitrine posés de front, sa: Head, neck and chest set facing out, without arms.
textes.Deux mains dextres qui se serrent, en fa: Two right hands clasping, fesswise by default; allegiance.
textes.Appaumée quand elle montre sa paume, con: Appaumée when showing its palm, contre-appaumée otherwise, blessing with two fingers (bénissante).
textes.De profil, en principe de sable, tortill: In profile, in principle sable, wreathed with a band.
textes.Nécessairement en armure et portant un é: Necessarily in armour and bearing a shield; on horseback, he is the Lithuanian pogonia.
textes.Torse nu et pagne en peau de lion ; ses: Bare-chested with a lion-skin loincloth; his columns mark the Strait of Gibraltar.
textes.Reconnaissables à leur nimbe et à leurs: Recognisable by their nimbus and attributes — the key for Peter, the sword for Michael.
textes.Trois jambes fléchies réunies en cœur pa: Three bent legs joined at the hip in the centre; the Isle of Man, Sicily.
textes.Terme rare pour la tête et le col, réser: A rare term for the head and neck, reserved for the stag.
An old name for the double tressure.
textes.La traverse du lambel ; par abus, le lam: The bar of the label; by misuse, the label itself.
textes.Les languettes du lambel, aussi appelées: The tongues of the label, also called gouttes or denticules.
textes.Pierre projetant huit rais, fleurdelisés: A stone casting eight rays, flory by default; pommetée, fleuronnée, allumée, percée.
textes.Champ semé de gouttes ; les gouttes peuv: A field semé of drops; drops can be of any tincture, tears are argent.
textes.Se blasonne d'un seul mot : il n'y a de: Blazoned in a single word: the only spots are ermine ones. Never “ermine” alone.
textes.L'adjectif correspondant à la vivre, lig: The adjective for the vivre, a sharp zigzag line.
textes.Mot passe-partout du blasonnement : « do: A catch-all word in French blazon: donjonné de trois pièces avoids repeating donjons.
textes.Autre nom du flanchis, le petit sautoir: Another name for the flanchis, the small couped saltire.
textes.Étoile à six branches, dite aussi didelt: A six-pointed star, also called a didelta.
textes.Meuble d'origine anglaise : un besant re: A charge of English origin: a bezant filled with azure and crossed by springs argent.
textes.Album illustré grand public (92 p.), réé: An illustrated album for the general public (92 pp.), reissued under the titles “Nouveau Guide de l'héraldique” (1984) and “L'Héraldique” (1992). Excellent for vocabulary and figures; on origins, its reading of “heraldry born of the Crusades” is now qualified by academic research.
textes.Ouvrage de référence de l'historien qui: The reference work of the historian who renewed the discipline. Cited here for the state of knowledge on the dating and origin of the system (12th century, tournament and seals), where the introductory work remains allusive.
textes.Guide pédagogique (224 p., ~650 dessins: A teaching guide (224 pp., about 650 colour drawings of coats of arms), the 2015 edition of a work first published in 2002. Used here as an additional source of facts, cross-checked with Joubert and Pastoureau; its illustrations, which are protected, aren't reproduced.
textes.Vue d'ensemble des ornements extérieurs: An overview of the external ornaments (helm, crest, mantling, coronets, supporters, motto), cross-checked with Boncourt's “Grammaire du blason” (wiesel.lu mirror).
textes.Sert de base à la description des couron: The basis for the description of French coronets of rank and for the comparison with the British peerage.
textes.Deux pages personnelles utilisées pour v: Two personal pages used to check the number of fleurons and pearls per rank. They don't agree exactly with each other or with Wikipedia (eight pearls in a row against sixteen pearls with nine visible for the count, for example): the disagreement itself is flagged in the article rather than arbitrarily resolved.
textes.Hiérarchie des titres et des fiefs sous: The hierarchy of titles and fiefs under the Ancien Régime (citing a treatise of 1764) and the break brought by the Napoleonic system and then the Restoration.
textes.Distinction entre manteau (souverains, p: The distinction between mantle (sovereigns, princes, dukes, peers) and pavilion (sovereign alone).
textes.Couleur et nombre de houppes du galéro (: The colour and number of tassels of the galero (ecclesiastical hat) by rank: cardinal, primate/patriarch, archbishop, bishop.
textes.Liste des six pairies laïques (Normandie: The list of the six lay peerages (Normandy, Burgundy, Aquitaine, Toulouse, Flanders, Champagne) and the six original ecclesiastical peerages (Reims, Langres, Beauvais, Châlons, Noyon, Laon).
textes.Principe général du chapeau à houppes («: The general principle of the tasselled hat (“the number of tassels is the greater as the dignity is more important”); the article gives no exact count for dignities below the rank of bishop, which is flagged as such in the text. Also provides the chain of texts that removed ornaments from episcopal arms, from the ordinance of 20 November 1611 to the instruction “Ut sive sollicite” of 31 March 1969, as well as the heraldic code of the Church of England.
textes.Édit de novembre 1696 : champ d'applicat: The edict of November 1696: scope, fee, article 12 on usurpation, the order of 22 July 1698 on fleurs-de-lis, arms by decree and the mechanical composition system of the order of 16 September 1701. The article carries a banner “does not sufficiently cite its sources”: the figures and examples repeated here are those referenced there (Borel d'Hauterive, Ciaudo, Loskoutoff).
textes.Décrets du 1er mars 1808 : passage des m: The decrees of 1 March 1808: the move of marks of rank from external ornaments into the shield, toques replacing crowns, chiefs and quarters by title, marks of office. Also useful for the distinction between rules of heraldic law and rules of blazon, and for the customary right of precedence.
textes.Formes d'écu : tournoi ou bannière, fran: Shield shapes: tournament or banner, ancient and modern French, then the so-called national forms (Italian “horse's head”, Swiss, English, German, Polish, Iberian).
textes.Chronologie des formes, de l'écu en cerf: A chronology of shapes, from the kite shield to the 17th century; the tournament shield with a notch (“à bouche”); Polish (16th and 17th centuries) and Italian shapes.
textes.Formes de pajzs en usage en Hongrie (ron: The shapes of pajzs used in Hungary (round, triangular, oval, hexagonal, tárcsapajzs, doborpajzs) and a warning about national labels.
textes.Les tarczas dites « nationales » et leur: The so-called “national” tarczas and their place in the evolution of the shield; refers to Szymański (2001).
textes.Définitions des croix nommées (Jérusalem: Definitions of named crosses (Jerusalem, Lorraine, Saint Andrew, Orthodox, Russian, calvary) and a gallery of variants. The figures used in the gallery of charges come from Wikimedia Commons and are credited one by one.
textes.Répertoire alphabétique d'environ deux c: An alphabetical directory of about two hundred entries, with sample blazons. The source of the definitions in the directory of charges and of the classification in three categories (charges unique to heraldry, highly codified charges, ordinary but frequent charges). The figures illustrating it belong to Projet:Blasons and are credited one by one when reused.
textes.Textes originaux en scots, lus dans leur: Original texts in Scots, read in their revised version. The first gives the Lord Lyon the power to visit, difference and matriculate arms, with confiscation and a fine for usurpation; the second ratifies this, creates the public register of arms of Scotland and sets the fine at a hundred pounds per offence. Parts repealed in 1906, a few words in 1987 and 1995; both acts remain in force.
textes.Organisation de la cour héraldique écoss: The organisation of the Scottish heraldic court: independent procurator fiscal, grant (administrative act) and matriculation (judicial act, with appeal). The FAQ page states that there are no “family arms” in Scotland and that clans have no arms.
textes.Compte rendu contemporain de l'affaire M: A contemporary report of the case Manchester Corporation v Manchester Palace of Varieties: facts, the two parties' arguments, the decision given at the hearing. Lord Goddard's reasoned judgment, delivered later, doesn't appear in it and has not been read here.
textes.Origine de la cour du connétable et du m: The origin of the court of the Constable and Marshal, the interruption after 1737, the revival of 1954. Cross-checked with Brooke-Little's report.
textes.Création en 1988 par lettres patentes, m: Creation in 1988 by letters patent, the Authority's missions (grants of arms, registration of historical emblems and those of First Nations, approval of Armed Forces badges).
textes.Article labellisé « bon article ». Date: An article labelled “good article”. The date of 4 June 1988, the text of the letters patent, eligibility conditions, fees, equality of women in transmission, protection of arms as a trademark.
textes.Ordonnance d'application de la loi du 3: The implementing ordinance of the law of 3 April 1919 (StGBl. 211/1919). Its § 2, no. 5, abolishes the right to bear family arms, “notably also those wrongly called burgher arms”.
textes.Vote unanime, rang constitutionnel, sanc: Unanimous vote, constitutional rank, sanctions and their extinction: Constitutional Court ruling of 9 October 2019 (E 1851/2019), cited but not read here.
textes.Le texte ne parle que du nom. Son extens: The text speaks only of the name. Its extension to arms comes from case law and is reported from the article “Wappenrecht”.
textes.Droit des armoiries en Allemagne, en Aut: The law of arms in Germany, Austria and Switzerland: free adoption, private rolls of arms, protection by analogy with the name (§ 12 BGB, art. 28 of the Swiss CC), Austrian ruling 6 Ob 649/93 of 1994. The decisions are cited from the article, not read.
textes.Définit la croix suisse (art. 1) et fixe: Defines the Swiss cross (art. 1) and fixes the red in an annex; reserves public arms for the community concerned and allows their use in reference works (art. 8); criminal penalties (art. 28). Replaces the law of 5 June 1931.
textes.Définition, puis la position d'une vingt: A definition, then the positions of some twenty authors from Palliot (1664) to Fernon (2019), who agree neither on the scope of the term nor on its legitimacy. The article carries “sources to link” banners (December 2024); only the positions it attributes by name are repeated here.
textes.Définition retenue par le Projet:Blasons: The definition adopted by Projet:Blasons, with a survey of authors who do or don't distinguish de l'un en l'autre and de l'un à l'autre: the article finds there is no consensus.
textes.Couleurs dites naturelles : « au naturel: So-called natural colours: “proper”, with its two special cases, carnation and tenné, reserved for realistic charges.
textes.Définition, procédés de brisure, brisure: Definition, methods of differencing, usual differences in France, how to read a differenced coat of arms, and the three systems of bastardy marks described by Laurent Hablot (2016). The article carries the banners “stub”, “sources” (August 2009) and “to be completed”, and a citation request for the “device system”; it relies on Duhoux d'Argicourt (1896), O'Kelly de Galway (1901), Fourez (1932), Grandmaison (1861) and Père Anselme with Potier de Courcy, whom we haven't consulted: only the points it states are repeated here, and disagreements with other sources are flagged.
textes.Les marques de cadence du système anglai: The cadency marks of the English system (nine sons), those of daughters and illegitimate children, the optional nature of the system in England — with statements by the College of Arms, Peter Gwynn-Jones and Oswald Barron — and its compulsory nature in Scotland. Two sections (“Background”, “Ways of differencing”) carry an “expand” banner (October 2017); only the points the page states are repeated here.
textes.Description du lambel, étymologie, évolu: A description of the label, its etymology, the evolution of its shape, its place on the shield and its change from eldest son's difference to younger son's. The article carries no warning banner; it has two references.
textes.Une définition par pièce : canton, franc: One definition per ordinary: canton, franc-canton, quarter (proportions “quite frequently found”, varying by author), pall, baton (three families of authors: Crayencourt, Pastoureau, Duhoux d'Argicourt), bendlet, filet, label. Authors' positions are repeated only as the page reports them. No warning banner; fourteen references.
textes.Termes de position et de disposition : e: Terms of position and arrangement: en abîme, brochant, sur le tout, sur le tout du tout, cantonné, sommé, surmonté… with examples. The page cites no source and carries no warning banner.
textes.Dictionnaire en ligne dont chaque entrée: An online dictionary each of whose entries reproduces definitions from old works, named but without page numbers: the entry for effaré cites O'Kelly de Galway (1901), Duhoux d'Argicourt (1899) and Maigne (1885), and notes that, for the horse, cabré is preferable. The works cited have not been consulted directly.
textes.Le champ et le fond, l'écu « plain » (et: The field and ground, the “plain” shield (and, more rarely, champé), paillé and diapered. The page carries the “needs sources” banner and cites no references: only the definition of “plain” is repeated here.
textes.Les champs remplis par répétition de pet: Fields filled by repeating small charges: the semé (indefinite number, incomplete charges near the edges, rule of tincture), paving (chequy, lozengy, masoned…) and its relation to furs. The page carries no warning banner and cites no references.
textes.Lexique des attributs qui modifient une: A lexicon of attributes modifying an ordinary, division or charge (alésé, bordé, bretessé, cléché, denché, fiché, pommeté…), each with its sample blazon.
textes.La position d'une figure (ce qu'on ne di: The position of a figure (what goes unsaid) and its attributes: animal attributes (armed, langued, pizzled, crowned…), attitudes of quadrupeds (rampant, passant, courant, sejant, couchant, dormant) and the rule of the crown, stated before the figure if of the same tincture, after if not.
textes.Le dragon à deux pattes des armoiries br: The two-legged dragon of British arms, distinct from the four-legged dragon, and the origin of the word (Anglo-French wivre, “viper”, hence also the French guivre).
textes.Définition de la pièce, distinction hono: The definition of the ordinary, the honourable / ordinary distinction (“very fluid”), five undisputed ordinaries, proposed objective criteria (surface, attachment, repetition) and the lists of four authors — Jouffroy d'Eschavannes (1855), Amédée de Foras (1883), Duhoux d'Argicourt (1896), O'Kelly de Galway (1901) — cited from the article and not read.
textes.Forme, position et rebattement du chevro: The shape, position and repetition of the chevron, chevronel and étai (with Duhoux d'Argicourt's minority view), attributes. Its origin and symbolism carry a banner “personal interpretation?” and aren't repeated here.
textes.Répétition de partitions ou de pièces si: The repetition of simple divisions or ordinaries: repeated ordinaries (odd number of zones) and alternating fields (even number), names of stripes (paly, barry, bendy, bendy sinister, chevronny) and their forms with small pieces (vergeté, burelé, coticé, étayé), default numbers. The article notes that the notion is defined in very different ways, is archaic, and that the term is less and less used.
textes.Blasonner des armes ou décrire une repré: Blazoning arms or describing a depiction, criteria of a well-composed coat of arms (attributed to the Commission nationale d'héraldique), the order of description of the shield and ornaments, examples (ancient Alsace, Liège, Dukes of Mayenne), intellectual property in French law. The article carries a banner asking for better sourcing of certain passages.
textes.Parti, écartelé, mi-parti, quartiers, gr: Per pale, quarterly, dimidiation, quarters, greater arms, chief of France; rules of blazon (the order “top before bottom, dexter before sinister”, cascade numbering); examples (Schönborn, Grenville diptych).
textes.Écus accolés ou écu parti ; usages franç: Accolé shields or a per pale shield; French and Belgian usages. A very short article, without references.
textes.Contourner un lion, une aigle, un heaume: Turning a lion, eagle or helm to look at the wife's arms; Alsace, Guelders, Montmorency. The article cites Fox-Davies (1909) and Bernhard Peter, not read here.
textes.Transmission des armes, femmes (héritièr: The transmission of arms, women (heiress, lozenge, widow), marriage, differencing; Scottish differences. Only the part on women and marriage is used in the chapter “Alliances”.
textes.Armoiries funéraires : panneau en losang: Funerary arms: lozenge-shaped panel, dark ground, oval coat of arms for wives, divided ground in the United Kingdom.
textes.Office d'armes : quatre grades, origine: The office of arms: four grades, origin in the 12th century, links with tournaments, golden age and decline in France (ordinance of 1306, college of 1406, judge of arms in 1615, last mention in 1830). The article refers to Nadot and Couhault, not read here; one of its sentences is marked “citation needed”.
textes.Types d'armoriaux (occasionnels, provinc: Types of armorial (occasional, provincial, institutional, general), dated examples (Bigot 1254, Compiègne 1278, Falkirk 1298, Gelre around 1430…), ordinaries of arms. No references in the body of the text.
textes.Fonction militaire du cimier, ornement d: The military function of the crest, a parade ornament, shapes according to the helm.
textes.Définition du cri de guerre, sa place au: The definition of the war cry, its place above the arms; a few French and Burgundian cries. Only the start of the article and a few examples are used.
textes.Définition de la devise, quelques exempl: The definition of the motto, a few famous examples, its place under the shield.
textes.Le listel : ruban portant devise ou cri,: The scroll: a ribbon bearing a motto or cry, under, over or around the shield.
textes.Définition et histoire de l'expression,: The definition and history of the expression, the right to the chief of France, the bonnes villes of the Consulate, the Empire (list of 1804, title of baron, annexations) and the Restoration (list of 1821: forty towns). The article cites official texts and historians' works (Chevalier, Favreau, Mauduech…), not read here.
textes.Décret du 17 mai 1809 et les trois ordre: The decree of 17 May 1809 and the three orders of towns with their marks (chief of bees, quarter, mural crowns). Only the introductory text is used; the armorial itself is a gallery of images.
textes.Origine antique de la couronne murale et: The ancient origin of the mural crown and its presence in municipal heraldry. A short article.
textes.Les procédés des armes parlantes et allu: The methods of canting and allusive arms, with many examples of municipalities and families. The article refers to Michel Pastoureau, “Une écriture en images : les armoiries parlantes” (2008), not read here.
